reason: E2 and E7 support the baseline brittleness from pile-ups and microcracking. E8 directly demonstrates L12 precipitation in FCC by low-temperature annealing in a similar eutectic HEA, with strength increase and maintained ductility. E5 provides evidence for back-stress hardening in hierarchical microstructures, though not specifically from L12 precipitates. The mechanism linking L12 precipitates to reduced pile-ups is not directly evidenced in the cited passages.
premises: Eutectic HEAs with FCC/B2 lamellar microstructure can suffer from dislocation pile-ups and microcracking at phase boundaries, limiting ductility.
Low-temperature annealing can precipitate coherent nano-scale L12 particles within the FCC phase of Al-containing eutectic HEAs.
Coherent L12 precipitates in the FCC phase increase yield strength without significantly reducing ductility.
Nano-scale precipitates can homogenize plastic deformation and reduce strain localization via back-stress hardening.
